### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aacf0c7ba0db3d16428246bc1ed82f8241b0b98d` — the merge of head `9d955a369a86c13a7047d2852fba3a9bda85f728` into base `89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aacf0c7ba0db3d16428246bc1ed82f8241b0b98d && git checkout aacf0c7ba0db3d16428246bc1ed82f8241b0b98d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e 9d955a369a86c13a7047d2852fba3a9bda85f728 && git checkout -B drift-repro 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e && git merge --no-ff 9d955a369a86c13a7047d2852fba3a9bda85f728

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 89f87f23440d61f8fcd10b2c2991c663a917181e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9d955a369a86c13a7047d2852fba3a9bda85f728`

### ① Derived judgments

- **The exemption predicate is "who may save this app": correct.** `RestServer.metaSaveVerdict(ctx, rawType)` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:3525`) calls `metaWriteCapabilityVerdict({ isSystem, systemPermissions, canonicalType: canonicalMetaUrlType(rawType), activeOrganizationId: ctx?.tenantId, operation: 'save' })`. That is byte-for-byte the argument set the PUT door built inline at the merge base. The read doors attach it as `mayWriteItem` in `metaReadAudienceSources` (`:3336`), from the same memoised `resolveExecCtx` result and the same `req.params.type`.
- **It is the PUT door's FULL caller admission: correct.** After the verdict, the handler (`:7244` onward) resolves the protocol (501 if there is no `saveMetaItem`), unwraps the body, and reads `If-Match`, `resolveMetaWriteActor`, `?force`/`?package`/`?mode=draft` and `organizationIdForMetaWrite(canonicalType, ctx?.tenantId)`. None of these refuses on a caller property.
  - `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` is `saveMetaItem`'s item/scope refusal, identical for every admitted caller.
  - `manage_org_presentation` is already folded into the verdict (an org-overridable type plus an active org, `packages/metadata-core/src/meta-write-capability.ts`), and `app` is not org-overridable. The census presenter edge drives the real PUT: `view` 200, `app` 403.
  - `endpoints.item` switches PUT, `/layers` (inside the `item !== false` block) and `/diff` (`registerPerItemRoute`) together, so it cannot turn an exempt reader into a refused saver.
- **The save door's own behaviour is unchanged: correct.** The diff replaces the inline call with `RestServer.metaSaveVerdict(ctx, req.params.type)`: the same inputs, and the same refusal envelope (`403 FORBIDDEN`, `verdict.message`). There is no unannounced write-path change.
- **The exemption applies only on the three stored-version doors, and only to `app`: correct.**
  - `mayWriteItem` has exactly three sites at head: the interface (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:65`), the app arm (`:1264`) and the transport (`rest-server.ts:3336`).
  - The transport supplies it only when `policy.app === 'author-exempt'` (`:3250`), and only `STORED_VERSION_DOOR_POLICY` (`:3502`) carries that.
  - The plain read and `/published` run `{ arms: 'all', app: 'gate' }` (`:7072`, `:8673`). `/history` and `/audit` run `eventDoorRefusal`'s `{ arms: 'per-caller', app: 'gate' }` (`:3407`).
  - The doc, book and dashboard arms never read `mayWriteItem`.
- **No author is served what the plain read refuses WHOLE: correct.** In the app arm, the `gated.app == null` refusals run before `serve(gateInputs.authorExempt ? document : gated.app)` (`:1300`): `permission` answers 403, and `unpublished` answers absent to a non-builder (ADR-0045 §3). In the census, author × `payroll` is 403 and author × `launchpad` is 404 on all six doors, and the scope pin enumerates those six cells as `stillRefused`.
- **The layered-view mechanism fix is correct, and neutral for other types.**
  - `serveMetaItemLayered` judges every present layer first, then assigns `served` (`:3949-3959`).
  - `serve(document)` returns the same reference for `doc`, `book`, `dashboard` (the `per-caller` skip), `object` and the default arm (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:1312-1361`), so the replacement is a no-op for them. The ADR-0106 mask runs afterwards, unchanged.
  - For `app`, a caller the plain read serves in full gets `filterAppForUserWithReason`'s copy (census `reader` × crm: every layer `toEqual(stored)`).
  - A residual nuance, not a defect: that filter also drops declared-empty `group` entries, so non-authors now get that tidy on stored doors, as the plain read already gives them.
- **The `/diff` mechanism fix is correct: it discloses less and reports no phantom deletions.**
  - `diffEmittedFrom` (`:3459`) maps each bucket in place, substituting only `value`/`from`/`to` from the judged sides. Bucket paths are preserved: the census asserts `bucketPaths(res.body) === bucketPaths(raw)`.
  - For unpruned sides, `diffSides` sets `to[path] = e.value` and so on, so the emitted values are identical.
  - A non-author loses the withheld entries' values on both sides. A `changed` entry can now show equal pruned values, which hides a change but never reports a deletion.
  - `object` is not `gatesPerCaller`, so its diff path is untouched.
- **The non-author fault path on stored doors is new, but identical to the plain read.** `resolveNavDocAudience` is now resolved for non-authors on stored doors, which it was not under `pending-decision`. A book-read fault drops `doc` entries (fail closed), which is the plain read's own composite answer. An edge pin covers it on `/layers`.
- **The runtime dispatcher is untouched, compiles, and behaves the same.** `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts:297` `RENDERED_DOCUMENT_POLICY = { arms: 'all', app: 'gate' }` is a member of the new union. The gate reads `ctx.mayWriteItem` only under `author-exempt`, which the runtime never passes. `git grep` finds no `pending-decision` anywhere at head.
- **The census reddens in every direction.**
  - Widened to `/published` for an author: the `pruned` row requires `navIds === plain` and no secret.
  - Widened to a non-author: `non-reader` × crm × stored doors requires no secret (PR ablation B: 5 red).
  - Widened to doc/book: the author rows are `refused`, with secrets forbidden.
  - Narrowed: the exempt cells require the secrets present and `toEqual(stored)` / `toEqual(raw diff)` (ablation A: 3 red).
  - `savesApps` is checked against the registered PUT handler with the real `metaSaveVerdict`: author 200 with `saveMetaItem` called once; `reader`/`non-reader` 403 `FORBIDDEN`; anonymous 401; the protocol is never called on a refusal.
  - The case count, 1+36+3+216+5 = 261, matches the file.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/rest` with `Clause-②: no` is correct, as ruling item 4 set.
- **Published surface:** the `@objectstack/rest@17.4.0` tarball, read from the registry, has `RestServer` 21 times in `dist/index.d.ts` and `MetaReadGatePolicy|MetaReadGateCaller|createMetaItemReadGate` 0 times. No file under `dist/` mentions `pending-decision` or `author-exempt`, and `dist/index.js` has 0 hits. The types enter the surface only through the still-pending `.changeset/20193-dispatcher-meta-read-gate.md` (`@objectstack/rest: minor`, on `origin/main`). So the combined release first publishes `'gate' | 'author-exempt'`, and nothing released moves.
- **Narrowing:** non-authors whom the plain read serves only part of an app now get it pruned on the three doors, where before they got it whole. That pulls a door back to a gate the contract already declares (`apps.mdx` "the entry is never served"; ADR-0046 §6.7; ADR-0045 §3). It is the same class three reviews upheld on PR #20190 as outside clause ②. No authorable accept set narrows, so no `(narrowing)` + BREAKING marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **THE DELIBERATE CORRECTION: `.changeset/20156-alternate-door-read-gates.md`** (on the merge base, `M` in this PR). Two spans are rewritten.
  - **Span 1, the bullet.**
    - Before (7 sentences): "**One case is unchanged in this release: an app the plain read would serve a caller only in part.** That is an app the caller may open, but with navigation entries withheld from them by `requiredPermissions` or the documentation audience. On `/layers`, `?layers=true` and `/diff`, such a caller still receives the stored app with those entries included, as before. No other caller does: an app the plain read refuses whole is refused on these doors too. What these doors should answer a partial caller is pending a decision, because both ways of matching the plain read restrict authors. Pruning the stored app would delete the withheld entries when Studio's designer saves back what it loaded. Refusing it would lock out any author who lacks one entry's permission, platform admins included."
    - (a) Sentences 1, 3 and 5 became false through this PR's behaviour change: the case changed, non-authors are pruned, and the decision is ruled. Sentences 2, 4 and 6 are true, but they are orphaned rationale or definitions that the new text keeps. Sentence 7 argues a rejected option and describes nothing in the release.
    - After, judged one by one:
      1. "For an app the caller may open, `/layers`, `?layers=true` and `/diff` answer by who is asking." (b) True: `serve(authorExempt ? document : gated.app)` under `STORED_VERSION_DOOR_POLICY`.
      2. "A caller who may save the app (the one `PUT /meta/app/:name` admits) receives the full stored version, including the navigation entries that `requiredPermissions` or the documentation audience withhold from them: Studio's designer saves back what it loads, so a pruned load would delete those entries." (b) True: `mayWriteItem = metaSaveVerdict(...).allowed`, the PUT door's admission; census author cells are `toEqual(stored)`.
      3. "Every other caller receives the app without the entries withheld from them, left out as the plain read leaves them out, on every layer and on both sides of a diff." (b) True: the per-caller arms (`requiredPermissions`, docs audience) run on each layer and via `diffEmittedFrom`. The per-deployment arms stay off, as the preceding bullet of the same note says.
      4. "The plain read and `/published` prune for every caller, authors included." (b) True: `{ arms: 'all', app: 'gate' }` at `:7072` and `:8673`; the census author × crm cells for the plain read and `/published` are `pruned`.
      5. "An app the plain read refuses whole is refused on these doors to an author too." (b) True: the refusals precede the exemption, and six author whole-refusal cells are pinned.
  - **Span 2, the closing sentence.**
    - Before: "…now receives the plain read's answer, except the `app` row of `/layers`, `?layers=true` and `/diff` for a caller the plain read serves only part of the app." (a) False now: only savers are excepted.
    - After: "…now receives the plain read's answer, except that a caller who may save an app reads it whole on `/layers`, `?layers=true` and `/diff`." (b) True of the combined release (#20190's pull-backs plus this exemption).
  - **(c) The rest of the note and the new changeset: nothing is false or contradictory.**
    - These hold at head: the frontmatter; the doc/book/object/dashboard bullets; `/history`/`/audit`; "`dashboard` is unchanged on every door except `/published`"; and "a caller the plain read serves in full gets the same answers as before".
    - The new `.changeset/20156-app-author-exemption.md` (`@objectstack/rest: patch`) agrees with the corrected note on every point, including that `manage_org_presentation` does not qualify (`app` is not org-overridable).
    - Observation only: the earlier bullet's clause "they show the stored version, which is what an author edits" is scoped to the per-deployment gates, and the corrected bullet refines it. It is not contradictory.
  - Deliberate correction of `.changeset/20156-alternate-door-read-gates.md` confirmed: 6 sentence(s) judged.
- **`content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` (:359-373):** every changed sentence is true at head:
  - "/published twin … to every caller, the app's authors included" (`app: 'gate'` on both);
  - "the one `PUT /api/v1/meta/app/NAME` admits: `manage_metadata`, or a system context" (the verdict is `isSystem` or `manage_metadata`, and `manage_org_presentation` is excluded for `app`);
  - "left out … on every layer and on both sides of a diff";
  - "lifts no whole refusal".
- **`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 49: true.** `metaSaveVerdict` holds an `isSystem` read (`ctx?.isSystem === true`), so a system context is exempt on the three doors. The anchor is added, and the count is regenerated from 87 to 88. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on head, so the census gate accepted it.
- **Files outside the claimed surface: none.** All 7 files are inside claim `5857413915` as amended in place: the gate, the transport, the census, the two changesets, `apps.mdx` and `system-context.mdx`. No runtime, metadata-core or spec file is touched.
- **PR body vs diff:** every mechanism claim is verified above: the copied ctx; the exemption gated on the policy, not the type; the layer replacement after judging all layers; diff emission preserving entries; `PENDING_DECISION`/`isPendingDecision` retired; the tarball's 0 hits; no runtime change. The first line is `Fixes #20156`, then a bare `Clause-②: no`. The objectui reader census and the ablation numbers are reported but not reproducible here (no repo attach was permitted), and they contradict nothing at source.
- **CI on head** (35 check-runs, all completed): 32 `success`; 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate` and `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, both rostered expected skips); 1 `failure`, `Check Changeset`.
  - The job log is not readable through the proxy (403).
  - By `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`'s diff-shape rule, the merge-base diff carries exactly one `M` row under `.changeset/` (the pending note) and one `A` row with non-empty frontmatter. So the only refusal it can raise is the foreign-changeset rule on the pending note: the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class this record confirms.
  - There is no other red.
- **Out-of-scope draft finding, server half: CONFIRMED at source.**
  - `GET /meta/:type/:name?state=draft` sets `state: 'draft'` on `getMetaItem` (`rest-server.ts:6988-7002`), then runs `metaItemReadGate(..., { arms: 'all', app: 'gate' })` with `visible = verdict.document` (`:7060-7068`).
  - No `mayWriteItem` is attached on that door. So an author lacking an entry's permission reads the draft pruned, while `/layers` serves it whole.
  - It is not this PR's required change; the carrier is the seat's decision.
- **The ruling's confidence gap:** the dev measured objectui's readers before the fix. It reports two `/layers` app readers, both of which save through PUT (the exemption's own predicate), and no `/diff` or `?layers=` reader. This was reported, not tolerated.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20156-app-author-exemption`
Reviewed-by: `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP`

### `Check Changeset` is red by design on this head: a confirmed DELIBERATE CORRECTION

<sub>`domain:cli` execution PM seat #6024 · session `session_01UYBdGBzWSrAMzpW8ah3GbP` · written 2026-09-27T18:58Z</sub>

- **The gate:** `Check Changeset` (`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, job `changeset-check`, which runs `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base "$MERGE_BASE"`).
- **The reason:** this PR modifies `.changeset/20156-alternate-door-read-gates.md`, a PENDING release note that PR #20190 added. The note's statement that partial `app` callers are "unchanged … pending a decision" is false once this PR executes ruling `5856774816`, so the PR corrected it in the same stroke. That is the gate's DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. Its own remedy text reads 「do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed」 and 「this gate stays red either way」.
- **The confirmation:** the at-tier contract review on this same head (`9d955a36`), record `5858783654`, names the note and judges each of its 6 rewritten sentences: 「Deliberate correction of `.changeset/20156-alternate-door-read-gates.md` confirmed: 6 sentence(s) judged.」 Under `landing-operations.md`, that record is the confirmation.
- **Why it does not block the queue:** `pr-automation.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only, with no `merge_group`, and `Check Changeset` is not a required context. Every other check on this head is `success` or a rostered expected skip.
